tvShow.name: Spartacus: House of Ashur
tvShow.overview: In a world where he survived the events of Spartacus, Ashur clawed his way to power, owning the same ludus that once owned him. Allying with a fierce gladiatrix, Ashur ignites a new kind of spectacle that offends the elite.

episodes.name: Dominus
episodes.overview: Having no memory of his downfall in "Spartacus: Vengeance," Ashur wakes to find himself the owner of the former House of Batiatus; eager to earn the respect and power he's always desired, Ashur must save face by presenting something new to the arena.

episodes.name: Forsaken
episodes.overview: Ashur navigates the treacherous waters of the Roman elites while Achillia struggles to acclimate to the brutal life of a gladiator in training.

episodes.name: Unworthy
episodes.overview: Korris faces Ashur's wrath and must prove himself worthy.

episodes.name: Blood and Bone
episodes.overview: Ashur frantically tries to enter the Ludi Apollinares games before Marcus Crassus arrives.

episodes.name: Goddess of Death
episodes.overview: Ashur presents Achillia to the public, where she faces her first battle in the arena.

episodes.name: Empty Things
episodes.overview: Ashur's popularity within Capua soars, but at a devastating cost.

episodes.name: Deepest Wound
episodes.overview: Korris demands blood; Ashur attempts to sway an enemy toward his cause.

episodes.name: Horizons
episodes.overview: Achillia prepares for her return to the arena, while Ashur faces a devastating setback.

episodes.name: Those Who Remain
episodes.overview: Caesar demands a painful sacrifice from Ashur.

episodes.name: Hail Caesar
episodes.overview: Achillia returns to the arena to face her greatest challenge, while Ashur wrestles with the emotional fallout of his actions.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
"Woketacus: House of DEI" is a truly horrible, sword and sandals parody, of the pretty decent original series "Spartacus" from 2010. Absurdly empowered, woke characterisations, look to re-write history, with yet another biology defying "girl boss", who somehow overcomes huge male gladiator killing machines, twice her size. Bringing a dead character, from the original story, back to life, doesn't enhance the series believability, either. 

In brief summary. There is little to like here. Decent sets and cinamatography, sure but its lipstick on a Roman pig. One to avoid.
